pr_title: Automatically mount encrypted swap partitions via gpt-auto
pr_body:
If the auto-discovered swap partition is LUKS encrypted, decrypt it automatically.

Fixes #20019

My C is terrible, so don't hesitate to point out anything ugly that I might be doing. I'm pretty certain the logic itself is solid (swap is picking up fine on my desktop with these changes).
pr_comments: I believe I've addressed all comments.

issue_context.title: Mount encrypted swap partitions with the correct partition type
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'm trying to move to a setup where I have no more hardcoded partition names into my `cmdline`.

This aligns very well with the [Discoverable Partitions Specification](https://systemd.io/DISCOVERABLE_PARTITIONS/), and by simply following it, I'm 90% there.

For most of the auto-discovered partitions, if the partition is LUKS encrypted, `systemd-gpt-auto-generator(8)` will handle unlocking them and accessing the volume inside of it.

However, for a `swap` partition, even if the partition type is set to `0657fd6d-a4ab-43c4-84e5-0933c84b4f4f` (the appropriate type), the partition is not unlocked:

```
# systemctl status dev-nvme0n1p3.swap
× dev-nvme0n1p3.swap - Swap Partition
     Loaded: loaded (/run/systemd/generator.late/dev-nvme0n1p3.swap; generated)
     Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since Thu 2021-06-24 17:25:36 CEST; 2h 42min ago
       What: /dev/nvme0n1p3
       Docs: man:systemd-gpt-auto-generator(8)
        CPU: 1ms

Jun 24 17:25:36 victory swapon[370]: swapon: /dev/nvme0n1p3: read swap header failed
Jun 24 17:25:36 victory systemd[1]: dev-nvme0n1p3.swap: Swap process exited, code=exited, status=255/EXCEPTION
Jun 24 17:25:36 victory systemd[1]: dev-nvme0n1p3.swap: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Jun 24 17:25:36 victory systemd[1]: Failed to activate swap Swap Partition.
```

It would seem that this specific partition type (and only this one) won't de-crypt the partition.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Partition should be unlocked with LUKS much the same was as other partitions (e.g.: `/` or `/usr`).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Using an unencrypted partition is a huge leak: the system will leave all kinds of sensitive material when powered off When suspending-to-disk, the entire RAM is copied into it.

Hardcoding the UUID into the `cmdline` defeats the purpose of the Discoverable Partitions Specification.

**The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for**

`systemd 248 (248.3-2-arch)`
comments: Yeah, automatically doing cryptsetup for encrypted swap is missing in gpt-auto. It's not difficult to do, it's just that noone spent the time on it so far.

I assumed it would not be very difficult too. I looked into `gpt-auto-generator.c` and `generator.c`, but it seems to be a bit beyond me.

I can't quite figure out what determines if partitions (e.g.: `/usr`) are LUKS encrypted or not. I may just have to leave it in the hands of those more adept at C :sweat_smile:

My workarounds for this have been flaky, so I'm wanting to give this another shot.

I'm thinking that in `gpt-auto-generator.c`, function `add_swap()` would need to:

- Read the partition, and check if there's a LUKS header.
- If the partition is missing, return non-zero.
- If there is a LUKS header, create two units:
  -  `systemd-cryptsetup@swap.service` that basically does `/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-cryptsetup attach 'swap' '/dev/disk/by-uuid/UUID_OF_PARTITION' '' ''`. I guess using `add_cryptsetup` does all the hard lifting here.
  - `sway.swap` that's basically a `systemd.swap(5)` unit with `What=/dev/mapper/swap`.
- If there's no LUKS header, do the same that's done right now.

Does that sound like an approach that would be acceptable?

Is there some existing function that would do the "check if this looks like a LUKS partition" part?

> I can't quite figure out what determines if partitions (e.g.: `/usr`) are LUKS encrypted or not.

libblkid shows the magic of a LUKS partition is `crypto_LUKS`

review_comments: Can there be multiple swap partitions? If so, this shouldn't be hard-coded
True. I'll do something like `"swap" + p->uuid`.
I think this should be something less likely to conflict and more self-explanatory. Maybe "gpt-auto-swap-<uuid>".

Actually the discoverable partitions spec documents the DM name to use for the partitions. It should be augmented to also do so for the swap device, and I thinkg the name /dev/mapper/swap is actually fine. I mean, we bypass all this anyway if there's any form of swap explicitly configured, hence I think the simple, obvious name is good, because it's not going to result in conflicts but be very very self documenting.

Indeed, DISCOVERABLE_PARTITIONS has various names like this: `/dev/mapper/root`, `/dev/mapper/tmp`, etc. Using `/dev/mapper/swap` is in line with this.

Nevertheless, I think the general approach is problematic. There is no conflict between various gpt-auto names as defined by us, but this namespace is not only used for this purpose. `/dev/mapper/` is shared for all device-mapper volumes, so not using any namespacing here is problematic. So I think all the names defined in DISCOVERABLE_PARTITIONS should be changed to `gpt-auto-*`. This would also make the whole scheme more obvious when used.

I am not sure I agree, I'd much rather stick to our defensive approach: use the obvious names, but whenever we see any sign that the user uses this otherwise step aside. i.e. if we find /dev/mapper/swap in fstab then we should step away.

I see nothing wrong with using the obvious names as long as we make it highly unlikely to cause a clash with this.

Renaming the devices is problematic since they are kinda API. If we change them this needs a really really strong reason, and I really don't see that here...

Yeah, renaming at this point would be complicated.

> we make it highly unlikely to cause a clash with this.

We are using some very short and "obvious" names in a shared namespace. "swap" is not so bad, but "tmp" is something that is very likely to be used for a different purpose by an admin.
What would be the issues with changing the mapper names? They are used internally by the generated mount units, no? As far as I can see it's the mount points that need to stay stable, no?

This will get freed when exiting the block by _cleanup_free_. Have an auxiliary `const char *path` that gets assigned the value of `what` in the above block instead, to avoid that, and use that below instead of `what`
Wouldn't that mean it's freed after the function returns? I don't see any lingering references to it.
Yeah, we don't want to free `p->node` here, this function doesn't own it
yeah, looks good - can you please squash all commits and force push?

This is not correct, the swap partition may be `swap` or `crypto_LUKS`.

By removing this assignment, it's set correctly near the end of this function. Without this change, the check in `add_swap` won't work.
